ch5_ex7_q1: The angle is over $45^\circ$, so the tree (opposite) must be taller than the distance to it (adjacent). An answer below 12.19 m makes sense.
To avoid dividing, use the angle at the treetop, $90^\circ - 54^\circ 22' = 35^\circ 38'$: distance $= 12.19 \times \tan(35^\circ 38') \approx 8.74$ m.
ch5_ex7_q2: Memory aid: depression means looking DOWN from a horizontal line, like feeling down. The angle sits at the top of the cliff, between the horizontal and the line of sight.
Small angle, long distance: $\tan 9^\circ 15' \approx 0.16$, so the boat is about $112 \div 0.16 \approx 700$ m away.
ch5_ex7_q3a: Estimate: $\tan 12^\circ \approx 0.21$, so the height is about $0.21 \times 830 \approx 175$ m.
ch5_ex7_q3b: Draw the lighthouse as a short segment stacked on the cliff. The trig height is the whole stack, so the cliff alone is the stack minus the top piece.
ch5_ex7_q4: The shadow is shorter than the post, so the sun must be higher than $45^\circ$ in the sky. That fits $65^\circ 46'$.
Shadow pattern: the higher the sun, the shorter the shadow. At $45^\circ$ a shadow is exactly as long as the object.
ch5_ex7_q5: Draw a horizontal line from the eye to the building. Trig gives the part above that line ($47\tan 17^\circ \approx 14.37$ m), and the eye height fills in the part below it.
ch5_ex7_q6a: Label the shared vertical side $h$ in both triangles. Two triangles with one common side is the signal to write two equations and set them equal.
ch5_ex7_q6b: Formula pattern for these two-point problems: $x = \dfrac{38\tan(35^\circ 50')}{\tan(47^\circ 12') - \tan(35^\circ 50')}$. Enter it in one go with brackets.
Check: substitute $x$ back into both expressions. Each should give $h \approx 82.82$ m.
ch5_ex7_q6c: Units: 180 cm is 1.80 m. A quick way to convert is to move the decimal point two places left.
ch5_ex7_q7a: Same set-up as any two-angle problem: the near point uses $x$, the far point uses $x$ plus the gap (here $x + 75$).
ch5_ex7_q7b: Shortcut formula: $x = \dfrac{75\tan(32^\circ 18')}{\tan(43^\circ 35') - \tan(32^\circ 18')}$. Typing it as one expression keeps every decimal.
Sense check: the nearer site is about twice as far from the building as the gap between sites, which is plausible for angles this far apart.
ch5_ex7_q7c: Check with the far triangle: $(148.37 + 75)\tan(32^\circ 18') + 1.89$ should give the same 143.10 m.
ch5_ex7_q8: One line: deck height above cliff $= 5800(\tan 16^\circ - \tan 15.7^\circ) \approx 32.8$ m. Factoring out 5800 avoids subtracting two big rounded numbers.
Why such a small angle change matters: over 5.8 km, a $0.3^\circ$ difference still covers about 33 m vertically.
ch5_ex7_q9: Height gained on a slope = length $\times \sin(\text{angle})$. So the cliff is $1500\sin 10^\circ + 1300\sin 20^\circ \approx 705$ m high.
The tree top is 150 m up, so the vertical drop to it is $705 - 150 = 555$ m, not 705 m.
ch5_ex7_q10: Since $32^\circ + 58^\circ = 90^\circ$, $\tan 58^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\tan 32^\circ}$. So the distances are $46\tan 58^\circ$ and $46\tan 32^\circ$.
ch5_ex7_q11a: Only the man's triangle (2.05 m tall, 1.5 m shadow) is fully known, so use it. Opposite is longer than adjacent, so expect an angle over $45^\circ$.
ch5_ex7_q11b: No trig needed: the man and the pole make similar triangles. Shadow tip to pole $= 1.5 \times \dfrac{3.08}{2.05} \approx 2.254$ m, so the man is $2.254 - 1.5 \approx 0.75$ m from the pole.
ch5_ex7_q12: The angle of depression from A to B equals the angle of elevation from B to A. They are alternate angles between two horizontal (parallel) lines.
ch5_ex7_q13a: Use a different letter for the eye height ($h$) and the part of the house above eye level ($x$). Mixing them up is the most common error in part b.
ch5_ex7_q13b: Estimate: $\tan 42^\circ \approx 0.9$, so the part above eye level is about $0.9 \times 15 \approx 13.5$ m. Adding 1.76 gives about 15.3 m.
ch5_ex7_q14a: Factor first: height gained $= 300(\tan 61^\circ - \tan 27^\circ) \approx 388.4$ m in 180 s.
To go from m/s to km/h, multiply by 3.6, because $1$ m/s $= 3600$ m/h $= 3.6$ km/h.
ch5_ex7_q14b: The balloon dropped, so the angle must drop below $61^\circ$. The new height (about 421 m) is still more than 300 m, so the angle stays above $45^\circ$.
ch5_ex7_q15: Use the complementary angle trick: the horizontal distances are $100\tan 50^\circ$ and $100\tan 28^\circ$ (measured from the vertical), giving a difference of about 66 m.
ch5_ex7_q16: Factor it: height $= 45(\tan 65^\circ - \tan 30^\circ) \approx 70.522$ m. The tall building is $45\tan 65^\circ$ and the gap above the short roof is $45\tan 30^\circ$.
Exact value: $\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so the drop to the roof is $\dfrac{45}{\sqrt{3}} = 15\sqrt{3} \approx 25.98$ m.
ch5_ex7_q17: Neat formula: height $= \dfrac{120}{\dfrac{1}{\tan 36^\circ} - \dfrac{1}{\tan 42^\circ}} \approx 451.5$ m. It comes from writing each distance as $\dfrac{h}{\tan\theta}$.
Check: Q should be about $\dfrac{451.5}{\tan 42^\circ} \approx 501.5$ m from the mountain, and P about 621.5 m, exactly 120 m apart.
